steps.summary: Multi-story European-style buildings with stone/brick facades lining a pedestrian street
Building on left with cream/tan colored facade and multiple barred windows
Building on right with grey/stone colored facade and regular grid of windows

Metal security shutter doors in tan/beige color at street level on left

Metal railings/barriers on balconies of buildings
White fabric or cloth object hanging on left building exterior

The phone numbers visible on signage (e.g., "55-12-21-50") use the Mexico City area code format (55-xxxx-xxxx), and "Cerería" (candle shop) signage is in Spanish. The architecture—ornate early 20th century stone/brick buildings with a mix of restoration and neglect, narrow pedestrianized cobblestone street, metal roll-down shutters, and modern Mexican traffic signals—is consistent with Mexico City's Centro Histórico, particularly streets like República de El Salvador or Correo Mayor which have this dense colonial/Porfirian mixed architecture and heavy pedestrian/bicycle traffic. The stone paving pattern and street lamp style also match those historic pedestrian corridors.
